title.narrative: Nexus support to Resident Coordinator Office

description.narrative: Nexusansatsen ska föra samman humanitära, utvecklings- och fredsaktörer för att på ett koordinerat sätt leverera mot gemensamme resultatområde. Dessa gemensamma resultatområden (könsbaserat våld, internflyktingsituation, tillgång till grundläggande samhällsservice samt ökad livsmedelstrygghet) är integrerade i den humanitära responsplanen, den nationella utvecklingsplanen samt MONUSCOs stabiliseringsplan. Målsättning är att på lång sikt minska de humanitära behoven och reducera sårbarheten hos de allra fattigaste och mest utsatta individerna i och samhällen. Denna insats bidrar därför direkt till att utjämna fattigdom i enlighet med det globala målet nummer 10: Minska ojämlikheten inom länder. Genom att koordinera mellan de olika pelarna av trippelnexus och inom alla de strategiska resultatområdena i Sveriges bilaterala strategi bidrar insatsen till att identifiera grundorsaker till konflikt och fattigdom och föreslå samarbeten som kan lösa dessa.

The Nexus approach funded through this contribution will bring together humanitarian, development and peace actors to deliver in a coordinated way towards Collective Outcomes. These Collective Outcomes (gender-based violence, internally displaced persons, access to basic public services and increased food security) are integrated into the humanitarian response plan, the national development plan and MONUSCO's stabilisation plan. The goal is to reduce humanitarian needs in the long term and reduce the vulnerability of the poorest and most vulnerable individuals and societies. This effort therefore contributes directly to reducing poverty in accordance with the global goal number 10: Reduce inequality within and between countries. By coordinating between the different pillars of the triple nexus and in all the strategic result areas of the Swdish development cooperation strategy, the contribution helps to identify root causes of conflict and poverty and propose collaborations that can solve these.

The project will support the coordination of development donors through a secretariat for the GCP - Groupe de coordination des partenaires as well as deploy a Nexus Specialist and two national nexus analysts who will work with humanitarian, development and peace actors across the spectrum to operationalize the collective outcomes in DRC.
The project will:
Support the DSRSG/RC/HC in coordinating the implementation of the humanitarian-development-peace nexus in the DRC. Provide advice and support to DSRSG/RC/HC, the UNCT and the HCT on scaling up humanitarian-development-peace interventions in light of the UN transition and MONUSCOs progressive drawdown in the Kasais and Tanganyika. Allow the DSRSG/RC/HC to be abreast on current Humanitarian-Development-Peace discussions and the New Way of Working at the global level, tools, instruments and policies as may be required.
In greater detail, according to the project proposal:
Scope 1: Assist and advise the DSRSG/RC/HC in coordinating the implementation of the humanitarian-development-peace nexus in the DRC
Expected Result: Effective coordination and convergence of activities in gegrophaical target areas across the three pillars of the nexus
Related activities:
- Support the DSRSG/RC/HC in ensuring better synergies of the development community with peacebuilding and humanitarian communities in the areas of analysis, planning, programming and financing.
- Coordinate and integrate different workstreams within the Integrated Office linked to the nexus.
- Provide secretariat function of the mutlistakeholder Nexus Core Team and support coordination with national/local authorities, State institutions, local civil society, private sector and development actors.
- Work closely with national counterparts, donors and other stakeholders of the humanitarian community including OCHA to ensure that humanitarian activities support and/or link into recovery and sustainable development strategies while ensuring that local capacity is utilized effectively.
- Advocate for the inclusion of early recovery and resilience building issues in the provincial operationalization of national humanitarian strategies and plans as well as in national and provincial development plans.
- Maintain close liaison with relevant development partners, the diplomatic corps, regional organizations and other actors supporting the UNs humanitarian, development, conflict prevention and peacebuilding efforts.
- Advise on funding opportunities and mechanisms to fund humanitarian-development- and peace related initiatives and programmes in fragile and conflict affected areas promoting durable solutions for returns, targeting the most vulnerable people, and actively advocate for donor support in this area.
- Support the implementation of the durable solutions strategy at national and provincial level (in cooperation with UNCHR and other relevant stakeholders).
- Organize and conduct workshops in Kinshasa and at the field level as relevant.
Scope 2: Provide support to DSRSG/RC/HC, the UNCT and the HCT on scaling up humanitarian-development-peace interventions in light of the UN transition and MONUSCOs progressive drawdown in the Kasais and Tanganyika
Expected Result: The humanitarian-development-peace nexus approach is scaled up in Kasai and Kasai Central and Tanganyika.
Related activities:
- Work with development and humanitarian partners, in particular UNDP, OCHA as well as MONUSCO/RCO and INGOs, NGOs and civil society representatives to facilitate the implementation and contextualization of the collective outcomes at the provincial level and the elaboration of joint strategies and interventions by the development community aimed at enhancing resilience, reducing humanitarian needs and facilitating a UN transition and progressive drawdown of MONUSCO.
- Establish coordination forum or provide support to existing coordination at provincial level to enhance the operationalization and rollout of the triple nexus approach.
- Provide support to mapping exercises of activities and efforts to enhance geographic convergence of implementation.
- Work closely with the PBF secretariat and other sections of the Integrated Office to ensure synergies between different projects aimed at supporting UN transition; provide advice on how to ensure a strong nexus focus in PBF funded projects.
- Maintain close liaison with the World Bank to ensure synergies with ongoing development programmes.
- Provide quality support to the development, implementation and evaluation of projects under the triple nexus.
- Organize and conduct workshops in the field as relevant.
Scope 3: Advise and inform the DSRSG/RC/HC on current Humanitarian-Development-Peace discussions and the New Way of Working at the global level, tools, instruments and policies as may be required
Expected result: Effective documentation and dissemination of best practices and lessons learnt from the DRC within the country and at global level.
Related activities:
- Maintain close contact with relevant staff in UN Headquarters as well at the regional level including relevant focal points at UNDP, OCHA, DPPA-DPO, DCO and work closely with the regional programme specialists based in the region.
- Contribute actively in a community of practice and ensure that lessons learned, and best practices are shared across a network of practitioners in order to strengthen the expertise in this area.
Compile best practices and lessons learnt from implementation in the Kasais and Tanganyika, disseminate within the country and feed into discussions at regional and global level.
- Perform any other duties considered necessary to advance the implementation of the humanitarian-development-peace nexus.
The above objectives remain the same for the component on nexus coordination however the following objectives have been added for GCP coordination.
Axis 1 Work between GCP members:
- Improve the functioning of the GCP through the establishment of a permanent technical secretariat,
- Strengthen joint donor initiatives on topics of common interest,
- Develop relations between partners, promote the exchange of information and data (political, economic, social and security, humanitarian and development situation),
- Contribute to the emergence of a common narrative and common positions in the field of development cooperation in general and sectoral policies in particular. Providing a coordination interface with the United Nations system
Axis 2 - Vis-à-vis the Congolese authorities:
- Support and develop high-level political dialogue with the Government of the DRC on development issues and other actors,
- Participate in the dialogue on cooperation policies and promote collective intervention through relevant initiatives, facilitating communication and exchange of information.

A. Rollout of the Humanitarian Development Peace Nexus
1. The SDG Leadership Lab on the nexus approach in DRC was organized from October 2023 to April 2024 and resulted in the cocreation of 4 prototypes[1]: (1) Activate a national steering mechanism for the nexus approach with the State at the center (2) Strengthen provincial nexus coordination (including durable solutions) around Governors (3) Promote a nexus culture (4) Implement nexus at local level (accountability to affected communities).One of the successes of this Lab was to confirm South Kivu and Ituri as the new provinces for the extension of the nexus approach (which had previously been questioned by some actors during the 2023 humanitarian scaleup).
2. The complementarity between humanitarian and development strategic planning processes was reinforced. For the first time, the analysis of 2024 Humanitarian Needs Overview and the Humanitarian Response Plan was included in the UN Common Country Analysis and made a distinction between: (a) Areas with a high level of vulnerabilities and significant humanitarian needs related to recent shocks (conflicts, displacement), which require a particular focus on promoting durable solutions and resilience for internally displaced persons and local communities. (b) Areas with a high level of vulnerabilities and chronic needs related to structural causes or past shocks, where development and peace interventions should be strengthened in complementarity with humanitarian interventions. This analysis was used to guide the strategy of the next United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), which is currently being developed for 2025- 2029. As a result, 3 products of the next UN country framework will be focused on durable solutions, social cohesion, and resilience, and will inform the programming of UN Agencies.
According to the 2024 chronic IPC analysis, the Kasai province improved from severe in 2016 to moderate in 2024. In Kasai Central, data from the 2023 acute IPC analysis showed that in the nexus pilot territory of Dibaya, there was a 15% decrease in the number of people in need between 2021 and 2023, thanks to a wide coverage by both humanitarian and development interventions. According to OCHA, the region no longer shows major signs of humanitarian emergency, and the needs and response are no longer primarily humanitarian in nature but are rather linked to structural issues requiring responses focused on resilience and development. In this context, close collaboration was maintained with OCHA until their Kananga (Kasai Central) office was closed in February 2024, and contributions were made to their exit strategy. In anticipation of the deactivation of the main humanitarian coordination (relais humanitaire), provincial governments heads of technical divisions were trained on nexus coordination and tools, to reinforce their capacity to coordinate and followup HDP interventions. Technical support was provided for the creation of the United Nations MultiProvincial Team (UNMPT) of the Great Kasai established in March 2024.
In Tanganyika, the provincial nexus coordination mechanism (involving UN AFPs NNGOs and INGOs and government) is functional at technical level, thanks to the dynamism of the Provincial Division of Planning and to the technical support provided by UNICEF from 2022 to 2023, and other key actors from civil society like NGO LIZADEL. At political level the Ministry of Planning has been involved for key decisions through the Technical Secretariat. With the recent appointment of a new provincial Governor (June 2024) and the arrival of the RCO Nexus Specialist based in Kalemie ( July 2024) conditions are in place to reactivate the nexus coordination mechanisms.
Two documents were published in June 2024 by the RCO: A note on Frequently Asked Questions on the HDPN in DRC and the first issue of an Information Bulletin the nexus approach in DRC. Experiences from the nexus approach in DRC were also documented in other reports such as: Integrated United Nations Approaches to Protection during Peacekeeping Transitions: lessons learned from MONUSCO" (CIVIC), The acceleration of the HDP nexus in the DRC (IE University).
In October 2024, a second mapping of good practices in the implementation of Humanitarian- Development- Peace Nexus approaches in DRC has been published by IASC and is now available online. According to this, some key milestones have been achieved in DRC such as the definition of collective outcomes, more coherence between key strategic plans, the establishment of provincial nexus coordination platforms chaired by local authorities, 3W mappings and joint results frameworks at provincial level. Contributing factors to this were: - The leadership of the tripplehatted DSRSG/RC/HC kept the nexus approach on top of the strategic agenda in multiple forums and in engagements with the Government, despite competing priorities with a specific emphasis on ensuring coherence and complementarity between analyses, strategic planning processes and evaluations. - The engagement of some bilateral donors throughout the launch and operationalization of the HDPN, including the existence of a Nexus Donor Group, has been instrumental in maintaining the nexus approach on the donors agenda, encouraging coordination among them, and catalyzing stakeholders interest for HDPN over the years. Through funding and advocacy, these donors have also encouraged HDP geographical convergence in the pilot provinces, and transversality of the peace pillar. - The commitment of provincial governments and technical divisions to take leadership and work together with the HDPN partners has enabled and facilitated consensus in the pilot provinces. - The dynamism of INGOs was also instrumental in strengthening nexus coordination platforms and encouraging the participation of local NGOs and civil society. - Geographical convergence over different programmes, through coordination and joint mapping of needs and gaps, has helped to adjust existing programming, create synergies in the same geographical areas and ensure complementarity of interventions with other partners across the three pillars. Flexible funding and innovative use of funds by operational stakeholders have been instrumental to the operationalization of the HDPN approach. - In nexus pilot provinces, some UN Agencies with a double humanitarian- development mandate leveraged different funding streams from multiple projects/donors or their own funds to create synergies in the same geographical areas. - Dedicated nexus staffing is crucial to support nexus coordination, provide ongoing advice and analysis on nexus operationalization, and inform key strategic and technical discussions related to the nexus.
B. Support to the RCO for the Group de Coordination des Partenaires (GCP) Secretariat
For the first time, an external evaluation of the GCP was organized with several stakeholders including the government, technical and financial development partners, leads and co-leads of Inter Donors Group (GIB sectoral donor groups) and civil society as well. The evaluation provided information on the current functioning of the GCP, including the process and recommendations for setting up a robust secretariat and GCP.
The GCP engaged in the follow- up the Global Partnership for Effective Development Cooperation. The GCP secretariat supported the government in the implementation of this exercise by providing stakeholders focal points and ensuring the participation of all development partners. The communication and the exchange of information with the Government were facilitated by the GCP secretariat. It conducted to several interactions between the GCP and the Ministry of Planning, which reinforces the collaboration. These relations led to the designation, in June 2024, of a focal point for the GCP for both the Ministry of Planning and the Ministry of International Cooperation. The GCP secretariat has also established an ongoing collaboration with the Directorate of Coordination of External Resources (DCRE) of the Ministry of Planning where we collaborate on the CCOAD decree (Framework for Collaboration and Orientation of Development Aid) for the implementation of the NAP, and the Global Partnership for Effective Development Cooperation.
The GCP secretariat has given impetus to the revitalization of the GTSs through exchanges with the Coordination Secretariat of the Thematic Groups (SCGT) of the Ministry of Planning. The first results is the update of the GTS synoptic table with updated information from the GIBs. The creation of a harmonization forum is being discussed as well. This exercise allowed the joint teams to highlight the differences and similarities between the GTSs and the GIBS, which require harmonization on both sides before a final decision on the number of sectoral groups led by the Government and the DPs.
To ensure a joint analysis of DRCs major challenges and issues, field missions were organized. The first took place from Tuesday 6 to Friday 9 February 2024 in Kalemie and Nyuzu in the province of Tanganyika, located in the southeast of DRC. The second joint visit was held in South Kivu, Bukavu, from Monday 27 to Friday 31 May 2024, with Government representatives with the participation of the Ministries of Planning and Foreign Affairs. These two visits made recommendations and proposed measures for the transition process in Tanganyika, the consideration of the Nexus approach, the continuation of the disengagement and transition processes in South Kivu, North Kivu and Ituri.
To contribute to the emergence of common positions in the field of development cooperation in general and sectoral public policies in particular, the GCP secretariat has begun to synergize with Development Partners by establishing first a regular collaboration with the GIBs to participate in GCPs monthly meetings. As a result, the secretariat launched the Digital Library where the GIBs can download their working documents. GIBs are invited regularly to the monthly meetings on a quarterly basis.
A broader multilateral engagement is also now in place at GCP level, and the AfDB, the World Bank and the IMF participate regularly in monthly meetings. Their presence is a capital contribution and constitutes an entry point for the GCP's advocacy through financial institutions to the government.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
